name: Global Privacy Platform string
plain: A coded record of a person's privacy choices for US states and other regions.
meaning: GPP replaces the US Privacy string. Its sections carry US national and state opt outs: section 7 for US national and 8 for California. Ad vendors read it via __gpp() to decide whether to sell or share data.

access.prompt_ui: CMP banner or opt out link
access.persistence: Stored in a first party cookie or storage by the CMP
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can carry your privacy choices for US states and other regions to ad partners
limits.user_action: You pick choices in a cookie banner or click an opt out link
can: Store your choices as a short coded string
Pass that string to ad and analytics partners
Cover several US states and other regions in one record
cannot: Force a partner to obey it, though laws may
Carry choices to a site you have not visited
Last if you clear cookies, since your choices may reset

story.what_it_is: A coded record of your privacy choices that ad companies read before they use your data.

marketing.name: Global Privacy Platform
marketing.pitch: The industry group says GPP carries privacy choices for many regions in one standard string for ad vendors.

story.for_you: You click a cookie or privacy banner. Behind the scenes, the choice becomes a short code that is passed to ad partners. You do not see it, but it should stop them from selling your data if you said no.
story.for_makers: Rules in US states and other regions now differ. One shared string saves ad vendors from building many different signals. It also gives regulators a way to check what the vendor knew.

use_cases.example: A news site records that a Colorado visitor opted out. Each ad bidder reads the GPP string and skips targeting.
A consent tool writes GPP on page load, and the tag manager reads it to block ad tags.
A free browser game site shows an ad auction that respects GPP for players in California and Virginia.
A video site passes GPP into the ad request, so streaming ads follow the viewer's choice.
A retailer uses GPP to decide if it can share purchase data with ad partners for a given state.
A privacy team keeps a log of GPP strings to prove it honored choices if audited.

risks: Only works if vendors respect it

technical_bounds: Section IDs defined by IAB (2 TCF EU, 7 US national, 8 California)
Does not by itself enforce the choice

legit_uses: Passing opt outs to ad tech
abuse: Ignoring opt outs by not reading it

history.change: US state laws begin using GPP sections
